channel.title: Paperraft
channel.description: Research in efficient inference and AI agents, ranked by independent GitHub implementations instead of citations or stars. Papers above the attention threshold are deliberately excluded.

item.title: DARE: Difficulty Analysis for Repair Enhancement
item.description: The method replaces uniform agent support and difficulty assessment based on solve rates with a framework that uses 151 static features to predict task failure rates and select task-specific support. It costs the engineering complexity of extracting feature groups and the computational expense of initially establishing ground-truth failure rates across multiple agents. It can fail if the moderate correlation (rho = .476-.621) misidentifies task difficulty, leading to mismatched support and suboptimal repair outcomes. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: coding agents. Recommendation: test.

item.title: When File Ingestion Misleads Language Models: Measuring and Mitigating Divergences in Office Documents
item.description: Prism replaces generic document text extractors that either expose hidden OOXML channels or drop visible content and reading order, causing models to see text diverging from what users view. It reconstructs the human-visible view from the OOXML specification before sending text to the model, with lightweight preprocessing overhead and no need to change downstream LLM APIs or infrastructure. What can fail is completeness across document formats or malformed OOXML files; if the reconstruction is imperfect or an extractor changes, hidden channels may still leak or visible content may be lost, so validation against your document types is required. 0 independent implementations, 3 stars. Research area: safety and guardrails. Recommendation: adopt.

item.title: Learning When Human Decisions Matter: Executor-Relative Consultation Value for LLM Agents
item.description: The method replaces ad hoc escalation rules, direct prompting about when to ask a human, and rollout-based value estimation at deployment with offline Monte Carlo executor rollouts distilled into lightweight predictors for budgeted consultation allocation. It costs offline rollout supervision, executor-dependent value estimation, predictor training, and added allocation complexity, while avoiding rollout-based value estimation during deployment. It can fail when the offline executor rollouts do not match the production executor or task distribution, when the human budget or consultation interface changes, or when value predictors misrank rare but high-impact decisions. 0 independent implementations, 20 stars. Research area: planning and decomposition. Recommendation: test.

item.title: A Hybrid Approach for Automated Security Pattern Recovery
item.description: SecPatRec replaces one-shot end-to-end LLM prompting for security pattern recovery with a ReAct-style agent that uses semantic and lexical code search for role detection and grounding, combined with static code property graph analysis for interaction recovery. The approach adds pipeline complexity and requires curated pattern reference architectures plus per-repository static graph construction, though it lowers LLM API costs relative to the baseline and handles repositories exceeding the baseline's input limit. Failures include incorrect role grounding when code search retrieves irrelevant entities, errors in statically derived interaction sequences (the weakest score at 0.66), and dependence on the availability of prescribed pattern role specifications. 0 independent implementations, 8 stars. Research area: coding agents. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Reglos: A Self-Evolving Personal Memory Agent with Recursive Self-Improvement
item.description: Replaces static memory stores and manually tuned retrieval harnesses with an append-only per-user memory whose context-assembly harness is iteratively patched by a coding agent and screened by a cross-family critic for benchmark overfitting. Costs are inference-only (training-free) but substantial: extra coding-agent and critic calls per patch cycle, a frozen evaluator stage, and dependence on a second model family for the critic, all adding latency and API spend. Failure modes include overfitting patches that pass the critic anyway, evaluator lock-in after freezing, memory growth from the append-only record, and gains that may not transfer to the reader's private workloads. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: memory and context. Recommendation: test.

item.title: SBVUL: Statement-Based Vulnerability Detection
item.description: Replaces function-level vulnerable/benign LLM classification with a two-agent pipeline that localizes and confirms exploitable statements using repository exploration and control/data-flow analysis. Costs multiple LLM calls per function (an exploration agent plus a per-candidate confirmation agent), implying significant API spend or infeasible latency on a single 24 GB GPU with open-weight models, and adds agent orchestration complexity. Fails by confirming candidate statements in 23–61% of patched functions and achieving at most 0.315 statement precision, so false positives remain high and the 200-pair benchmark may not transfer to other codebases. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: coding agents. Recommendation: test.

item.title: HarnessFlow: MCTS-Guided Harness Optimization for LLM Agents
item.description: HarnessFlow replaces the manual, ad-hoc design of agent scaffolding and tool-use loops with an automated Monte Carlo Tree Search over executable harness code. The approach requires a budget of approximately 15 end-to-end evaluation cycles per task and the operational cost of running a coding agent to generate and test candidate harnesses. Reliance on archived execution history can lead to overfitting to specific benchmarks or failure to generalize to unseen environments, and the MCTS search may converge on suboptimal harness designs if the evaluation budget is too constrained or the coding agent produces buggy code. 1 independent implementation, 23 stars. Research area: tool use. Recommendation: test.

item.title: CLEAR: Structured Specifications for Controllable Long-Horizon ML Research Engineering
item.description: The paper proposes CLEAR, which replaces the implicit, free-form interpretation of research artifacts with structured specifications that an agent maintains while translating papers into executable ML systems. The cost is an additional specification-authoring and maintenance layer on top of agent execution, plus orchestration complexity, with no quantified gain reported in the abstract. It can fail if the specification is wrong or incomplete, if the agent drifts from it during long execution, and because automating full research-to-system workflows typically demands repeated long training and evaluation runs that exceed a single 24 GB GPU and a limited cloud budget. 0 independent implementations, 1 star. Research area: planning and decomposition. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Scalable Bayesian Gaussian Process Classification for Cancer Histopathology: Calibrated Uncertainty Under Distribution Shift
item.description: The method replaces neural-network and stochastic variational GP classifiers for calibrated pathology prediction by running HMC-based low-rank Gaussian Process Classification on frozen Phikon foundation-model embeddings. It costs the infrastructure to extract embeddings at scale, a low-rank kernel factorization via RPCholesky, and HMC posterior sampling over roughly 300,000 points, which is heavier than a single deterministic classifier and adds implementation and tuning complexity. It can fail when the frozen embeddings are mismatched to a target hospital, when kernel or likelihood choices are poorly specified, or when the low-rank approximation discards structure needed for rare subgroups, despite improved reported calibration. 0 independent implementations, 4 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Bayesian Tensor Train Kernel Machines with Automatic Model Complexity Inference
item.description: Replaces deterministic tensor-network kernel machines with manually tuned TT ranks and feature dimensions by inferring both through hierarchical ARD priors and mean-field variational inference. Costs the same asymptotic complexity as deterministic alternating least squares but adds probabilistic bookkeeping, requires an over-parameterized initialization, and remains a kernel machine whose cubic-in-samples scaling persists unless the underlying kernel solver is approximated. Can fail when mean-field assumptions misrepresent core couplings, when the ARD pruning is sensitive to prior hyperparameters, or when datasets are large enough that exact kernel methods are impractical regardless of tensor compression. 0 independent implementations, 3 stars. Research area: efficient training. Recommendation: test.

item.title: More Agents, More Reliable? System-Level Reliability of Multi-Agent LLMs under Operational-Profile Uncertainty
item.description: It replaces average benchmark accuracy and agent-count heuristics with a reliability envelope that propagates imprecise agent failure probabilities through a Bayesian network of system failure logic. The cost is extra modeling and evidence requirements: you must estimate interval failure probabilities, specify the combining rule and its failure modes, and maintain the assessment as the operational profile changes. It can fail if the input mix is mischaracterized, the merger/voter failure logic is wrong or correlated failures are ignored, or intervals are too wide to support deployment decisions. 1 independent implementation, 14 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: test.

item.title: FastAFD: When Does Attention-FFN Disaggregation Pay on Rack-Scale NVLink?
item.description: It replaces colocated wide expert parallelism for large MoE decode by splitting attention GPUs from expert GPUs and overlapping one microbatch's MoE with the other's attention. The cost is dedicating GPUs to experts, added scheduling and communication complexity, and hardware assumptions tied to rack-scale NVLink systems. It can fail when the batch and overlap gains do not exceed the disaggregation cost, as shown by parity on MiniMax-M2.5 and by workloads unlike the profiled serving regime. 1 independent implementation, 123 stars. Research area: serving and batching. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Multi-step SWE: Can Coding Agents Keep Building on Their Own Code Over Long Horizons?
item.description: This benchmark replaces single-task coding evaluations with 69 long-horizon tasks, each a chain of 5-15 dependent steps on one codebase, testing whether agents can build on their own prior code. It costs the effort of running multi-step evaluations and integrating verifier-based scoring into your testing pipeline, but requires no additional training or hardware beyond standard inference. Long-horizon agent chains can fail through compounding errors: early design mistakes persist, and even frontier models solve only 18.5% of tasks, so production deployments need human review and cannot assume autonomous multi-step reliability. 1 independent implementation, 24 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: SeVerus: Context-Aware, Gamified Benchmarking for Rust Verification
item.description: It replaces Verus benchmarks that hand agents the auxiliary lemmas by generating quests whose levels progressively remove proof context while a checker guards executable code, specifications, and proof soundness. Adoption costs Verus project selection, quest generation, independent checking, noisy binary-search evaluation, and rising agent API spend as context is withdrawn. It can fail as a production signal if the reader does not verify Rust code, if longer-quest failures are the real target, or if agents pass by alternative decompositions rather than recovering the withheld lemmas. 0 independent implementations, 4 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Capability Gain from ISA to Shared Execution on AMD MI300A and MI250X
item.description: Replaces ad-hoc peak-throughput comparisons with a metric tracing instruction-level gains through libraries, applications, and shared queues, applied to AMD MI300A vs MI250X. Requires CDNA3 hardware with FP8 and 2:4 sparse instructions plus vendor-library support; quantization must be fused into GEMMs to avoid overhead. Fails in production when unfused quantization makes FP8 a per-layer slowdown in LLM inference, when sparsity library support captures only half the theoretical gain, and when queue-shared serving gains nothing from lower precision. 0 independent implementations, 4 stars. Research area: quantization. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: τ-bench-LILT: Evaluating Conversational Agents on Realistic Multilingual Tool-Use Tasks
item.description: The benchmark replaces English-only tool-use agent evaluation (tau-bench/tau^3-bench) with natively localized variants spanning German, Korean, Turkish, and Farsi across airline, retail, telecom, and banking domains, including culturally appropriate databases and native-expert-refined user simulators. Adoption costs the engineering effort of running the benchmark harness against the production agent and, for languages beyond those released, replicating the native-speaker localization process rather than machine-translating prompts. It can fail by overfitting agent tuning to benchmark-specific phrasings, and its fixed domain set may not cover the reader's actual production tools or languages. 4 independent implementations, 161 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Not All Loops Cost the Same: Phase-Dependent Depth for Serving Looped Transformers
item.description: LoopDuet replaces uniform loop budgets in serving looped transformers with phase-dependent depth selection for prefilling and decoding. It costs implementation complexity in vLLM for token gathering and a queue-age controller, but uses existing weights and kernels. It can fail if the adaptive prefilling does not retain quality under varying demand or if the specific looped transformer models are not available. 0 independent implementations, 4 stars. Research area: serving and batching. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: TileQuant: Tile as the Precision-Allocation Unit for LLM Mixed-Precision Post-Training Quantization
item.description: TileQuant replaces uniform-weight PTQ and column-wise mixed-precision retention with precision assignment at hardware-aligned 2D tiles, keeping only the highest-sensitivity tiles at 16-bit and quantizing the rest to 8-bit using offline calibration and a custom kernel. It costs an offline calibration and weight-reconstruction pass, a nonstandard kernel and buffer layout to integrate and maintain, and partial (16-bit) storage for retained tiles, so compression is below pure 8-bit. It can fail if calibration statistics do not transfer to production data, if the custom kernel underperforms or lacks support on the reader's specific GPU, or if retained-tile budgets are mis-set, degrading quality without recovery at runtime. 1 independent implementation, 4 stars. Research area: quantization. Recommendation: test.

item.title: SPILLWAY: Separating Target Admission from Sanitization to Defend Tool-Using Agents against Prompt Injection
item.description: SPILLWAY replaces per-task LLM-based planning or routing for security with a deterministic admission check that validates tool-call targets against typed fields from read-only tools, plus a rule-based sanitizer that strips instruction-like regions before the model sees them. It costs implementation complexity: defining typed tool schemas, fixed delegation rules, sanitizer patterns, and an optional local judge, but adds almost no model-call overhead or latency. It can fail if attacks evade the fixed sanitizer rules, if delegation rules are misconfigured, or if legitimate targets are refused and the local judge errs, and it only defends against target-redirection, not other attack classes like data exfiltration through allowed targets. 3 independent implementations, 7 stars. Research area: safety and guardrails. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Recursive Sparse Attention: Million-Token Length Extrapolation at Logarithmic Cost
item.description: Replaces dense attention over the full KV cache with a hierarchical tree that summarizes the cache using distilled pooling keys, selecting tokens at logarithmic cost. Requires training a pooler per layer on 0.62B tokens and deploying custom optimized kernels; adds complexity to the inference stack and requires distillation from the target model. Failures can occur if the pooler misses relevant long-range dependencies or if custom kernels contain implementation bugs that affect production stability. 1 independent implementation, 129 stars. Research area: attention and kernels. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: How Do AI Agents Waste Your Money?
item.description: The method replaces aggregate token-limit monitoring with trajectory-level waste identification, using an LLM-as-a-Judge to flag removable reasoning spans before or during execution. It requires recording complete agent trajectories, normalizing heterogeneous formats, and adding LLM judge calls that incur additional token costs and integration complexity. The approach can fail if the judge incorrectly labels necessary reasoning as waste, leading to degraded task performance when spans are removed. 3 independent implementations, 139 stars. Research area: coding agents. Recommendation: test.

item.title: TriAttention: Unified Sparse Mixed-Precision Attention for Long-Context LLM Inference
item.description: Replaces dense BF16 attention and its full-precision KV cache with tile-level triage that skips, 4-bit, or 8-bit computes QK tiles, plus a compressed quantized KV cache reused at decode. Costs include an offline per-head calibration and budget allocation pass, a fused custom kernel, and possible quality loss on workloads whose attention patterns do not match the diagonal-boundary policy. Can fail when the two-boundary head representation misses irregular critical interactions, when the fused kernel does not support the deployment stack, or when speedups do not materialize at the short contexts typical of the reader's traffic. 0 independent implementations, 4 stars. Research area: attention and kernels. Recommendation: test.

item.title: HyFlash: A Prefix-Memory Prior for On-Device Speculative Decoding
item.description: HyFlash replaces full-context attention in parallel block drafters for speculative decoding with a hybrid design: local attention over recent context plus a fixed-size recurrent memory that compresses historical target features, bounding draft-side KV storage. The cost is added drafter architecture complexity and the need to implement or adopt a nonstandard drafter rather than reuse an off-the-shelf small model; the abstract reports higher acceptance and lower KV storage but gives no quantified speedup. It can fail if acceptance gains do not transfer to the reader's target model and workload, if no maintained implementation exists, or if integration overhead with an existing serving stack exceeds the drafting benefit. 1 independent implementation, 129 stars. Research area: speculative decoding. Recommendation: test.

item.title: How Should Agents See Code? Rethinking Code Representations for Agentic Software Engineering
item.description: The technique replaces raw-file and lexical-search repository access with queryable repository maps (ASTs, call graphs, module dependencies, documentation-enriched search, or hybrids) that agents consult during tasks. It costs additional latency on some benchmarks, increased token usage on test-generation tasks, and engineering effort to build and maintain the repository indexes. Benefits are task-dependent: gains are strongest for localization bottlenecks and narrow or vanish when patch or test authoring is the decisive step. 0 independent implementations, 4 stars. Research area: coding agents. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Provably Efficient Representation Learning for Low-Rank CMDPs
item.description: The method replaces model-based approaches for constrained Markov decision processes by combining LSVI-UCB with primal-dual optimization to avoid explicit transition kernel estimation. It requires learning representation vectors and value function mappings with bonus terms for uncertainty, adding implementation complexity. The theoretical guarantees depend on the low-rank CMDP assumption and unknown feature representations, which may not hold in standard LLM or ML systems; the approach is designed for sequential decision-making under constraints, not generative AI or typical ML inference tasks. 0 independent implementations, 4 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: not applicable.

item.title: Take It From Here: Evaluating Coding Agents On Project Takeover
item.description: ReqMemBench replaces generic single-turn coding benchmarks with an evaluation that provides interaction history, the pre-request project environment, and a new request, then validates takeover via delivery tests and requirement-atom diagnostics. It costs the construction of curated interaction histories, executable project environments, and delivery tests, plus harness integration and evaluation compute on the reader's 24 GB GPU or API budget; it adds no serving latency but requires maintaining requirement-state annotations. It can fail to transfer if the reader's production histories, stacks, or request types differ from the 37 executable targets, and its diagnostic labels may not capture all failure modes; low absolute delivery rates also limit its use as a regression gate without task-specific calibration. 2 independent implementations, 17 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: test.

item.title: From What Is Used to What Is Missing: Rethinking Dynamic Rank in LoRA
item.description: GEAR replaces static or heuristic dynamic-rank allocation in LoRA with a tangent-normal decomposition that estimates the normal-space spectrum to guide locally optimal rank expansion and task-induced initialization. The cost is added implementation complexity and matrix-free spectral estimation overhead during training, while reduced trainable parameters lower optimizer memory on a 24 GB GPU. It can fail if the local quadratic assumption poorly approximates the loss landscape, if matrix-free normal-spectrum estimates are noisy, or if gains observed on evaluated language and vision benchmarks do not transfer to the reader's tasks and models. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: efficient training. Recommendation: test.

item.title: EnvOpt: Automated Optimization for Agent Environments
item.description: EnvOpt replaces hand-designed agent environments (tool outputs, document layouts, data-source representations) with automatically optimized environment configurations, requiring no graders or reference answers and using real or synthetic tasks. The cost is an offline optimization loop that consumes API or GPU inference budget, plus the engineering effort to expose the environment as a tunable surface and to build representative tasks. It can fail when the synthetic or sampled tasks do not match the production task distribution, when the optimized environment overfits to one benchmark and degrades under environment drift, or when undocumented rejected strategies silently hurt accuracy on unseen task types. 5 independent implementations, 161 stars. Research area: tool use. Recommendation: test.

item.title: CacheGraft: Enhancing Retrieval-Augmented Generation via Latent-Space Document Enrichment
item.description: The method replaces standard text-based retrieval augmentation with a fused KV cache representation generated offline by a larger sharer model, which is injected directly into the latent space of a smaller receiver model at query time. It costs the storage and offline computation required to encode each corpus passage into a fused KV cache representation. This approach can fail if the zero-shot fuser does not generalize to the specific retrieval data, or if the statistically insignificant improvements in 13 of 30 comparisons fail to manifest as real-world gains. 1 independent implementation, 4 stars. Research area: retrieval and RAG. Recommendation: test.

item.title: FINCOSMOS: An Open-World Evaluation Paradigm for Agents in Finance
item.description: It replaces fixed-task, fixed-data, or fixed-timeline financial benchmarks that cannot expose silent failures such as unrequested strategies, unverified web data, or lookahead bias. The cost is substantial evaluation complexity: a simulated user, hidden strategy grammar, live web data acquisition, cutoff enforcement, recomputation of metrics, and multiple veto checks. After adoption, it can fail by being too expensive or slow for routine regression testing, overfitting agent behavior to this benchmark family, or still missing production failures outside finance-specific web backtesting. 1 independent implementation, 14 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: test.

item.title: ZYFA: Speed and Accuracy of FP8 FlashAttention on AMD CDNA4
item.description: ZYFA replaces the vendor AITER FP8 attention kernels on AMD MI355X with a custom prefill kernel that approximates the softmax exponential with a multiply-add plus integer conversion, uses a ping-pong schedule to overlap softmax with matrix multiplies, and rescales probability blocks by powers of two before rounding. It costs adoption of a research-grade kernel tied to a single GPU architecture (CDNA4/MI355X), with added implementation complexity and dependence on instruction ordering rather than hardware synchronization. It can fail through throughput variability because the MI355X sustained clock depends on operand values, so benchmark gains on random inputs may not transfer to production activations, and it offers no benefit on NVIDIA hardware. 0 independent implementations, 4 stars. Research area: attention and kernels. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: RLGPA: A Reinforcement Learning-Guided Granularity Planning Attack for Decision-Based Sparse Adversarial Examples
item.description: RLGPA replaces heuristic or fixed-policy strategies for sparse adversarial example generation with an online reinforcement learning scheduler that dynamically selects support-reduction executors and granularity. The method incurs the cost of training a Dueling Double DQN planner and managing state-conditioned action masking, which increases implementation complexity compared to baseline attacks. Success depends on the availability of a decision-based oracle and may fail if the victim model changes its labeling behavior or if the query budget is insufficient for the RL policy to converge. 0 independent implementations, 2114 stars. Research area: safety and guardrails. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: SPARE: Fast Linear Attention Decoding with Compact Recurrent States
item.description: SPARE replaces dense recurrent states in linear attention with compact, low-dimensional projections, performing reads and updates directly on these compressed states without dense reconstruction or online decomposition. It requires careful heterogeneous rank allocation and write compensation to preserve associative-retrieval accuracy. The primary risk is that aggressive rank reduction or improper subspace selection may degrade retrieval performance below acceptable levels for specific workloads. 1 independent implementation, 129 stars. Research area: efficient architectures. Recommendation: test.

item.title: SKIM: Pruning Large Language Model Agents via Selective Knowledge Informed Masking
item.description: It replaces conventional unstructured or magnitude-based pruning and standard distillation with token-role partitioning that drives category-aware saliency scores, valid-token alignment, and feature matching for grammar-constrained generation. The cost is a two-stage pruning and distillation pipeline that requires teacher inference, training compute, and logic to identify and maintain token roles. It can fail if token categorization is inaccurate, if the structured grammar changes, or if high sparsity damages capabilities not covered by the tool-calling benchmarks. 1 independent implementation, 135 stars. Research area: sparsity and pruning. Recommendation: test.

item.title: OpenRDMA: A GPU-Native Multi-Path Reliable RDMA Transport Architecture
item.description: OpenRDMA replaces CPU-mediated GPUDirect RDMA control paths and SM-consuming IBGDA WQE assembly with an FPGA NIC that reconstructs Work Queue Entries from an 8-byte GPU-issued doorbell token, adding multipath reliable transport with out-of-order delivery and CPU-managed retransmission. It costs custom FPGA hardware, preconfigured WQE context management, and a hardware-software split that shifts timeout and recovery complexity to CPU software, with no published performance numbers since the prototype is still under implementation. Adoption can fail because the design targets large-scale multi-node AI clusters with specialized NICs, provides no benefit on a single-GPU or API-based setup, and its reliability and performance remain unvalidated absent a working prototype. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: not applicable.

item.title: ACSeL: Adaptive Configuration Search for Hardware-Constrained LLM Inference
item.description: It replaces manual or exhaustive tuning of model size, batch size, quantization algorithm, and mixed-precision layer assignments under memory and latency SLOs. It adds implementation and calibration overhead, depends on a small calibration corpus and profiling, and may sacrifice quality if RMQD misestimates downstream performance or FMC mis-calibrates latency. Feasibility can fail when operator-profile latency estimates do not transfer across kernels, batch sizes, or hardware, or when the chosen quantization recipe behaves differently in production than in calibration. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: quantization. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Stress Testing Chain-of-Thought Monitoring Against Covert Misalignment
item.description: Replaces single-pass chain-of-thought monitoring with a Bayesian trajectory monitor that fuses global context with local segment evidence, hardened against red-teamed trace-shaping attacks. Costs additional monitor inference over segmented traces plus integration and calibration effort, and likely depends on frontier API monitors (GPT-5.2, Claude-4.5) rather than a self-hosted 24 GB model. Can fail against adaptive evasions outside the TraceMRT attack distribution, and the 0.74 TPR at 5% FPR means roughly one in four covert trajectories is still missed. 2 independent implementations, 2239 stars. Research area: safety and guardrails. Recommendation: test.

item.title: TACT-KV: Tri-Axis Cosine Transform for Compressing Volumetric KV Caches in Medical VLMs
item.description: TACT-KV replaces standard full-precision or token/feature-statistics-based KV cache compression with a calibration-free separable 3D discrete cosine transform applied to the KV cache, followed by reverse-water-filling bit allocation across frequency bins and fixed-codebook scalar quantization. It costs an additional transform/inverse-transform step on KV states per layer (modest compute and implementation complexity) and introduces quantization distortion that is only bounded by spectral concentration of the cache; at aggressive 1-bit budgets some prediction flips still occur. It can fail when KV energy is not spatially concentrated along anatomical axes, when workloads lack 3D spatial structure, or when the method is applied to models or tasks whose accuracy is sensitive to low-bit frequency truncation, since gains were validated mainly on 3D medical imaging and video tasks. 0 independent implementations, 125 stars. Research area: KV cache. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Evolver: Turning Agent Exploration into Evolving Capabilities
item.description: The method replaces transient agent execution traces with persistent structured Gene assets that encode procedural experience and are retrieved to condition future executions without updating foundation model parameters. Its cost is additional retrieval infrastructure, asset storage and curation, plus overhead for feedback-guided evolution, while model training remains unnecessary. Failures can occur if retrieved Genes drift from the task domain, if retrieval injects misleading procedures, or if benchmark-specific gains do not transfer to production workloads. 0 independent implementations, 20 stars. Research area: memory and context. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Beneath the Surface: What We Overlook When We Talk About Agent Evolution
item.description: This method replaces relying on a single benchmark score or simple best-score admission for evolving agent harnesses with preservation-aware evaluation, explicit applicability conditions, and tested decision rules, plus EvoAudit-style revisions to select, analyze, mutate, and gate. It costs extra evaluation runs, controlled agent expansion, component interventions, admission replays, and more complex release criteria, and most reliability gains increase deployment cost. It can fail because all evolved agents gained some tasks while losing others, component benefits can change when combined, stricter admission can discard useful alternatives, and transfer often preserves gains only selectively across harnesses and task domains. 2 independent implementations, 138 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: test.

item.title: The Gating Mechanism of KV Cache Eviction
item.description: It replaces heuristic or score-based KV cache eviction policies (and naive learnable gates trained on LM loss) with a gate placed inside the attention softmax, trained against the frozen dense model's predictions rather than the language-modeling objective, plus parameter-free centroids that return evicted mass within the same normalizer. The cost is a training pass for the gate on a frozen 8B-scale backbone (feasible on one 24 GB GPU with offloading or parameter-efficient setups), added inference complexity from centroid handling, and roughly 1.4-3.7 benchmark points of quality loss at 4x cache compression. It can fail on workloads where the gate's training distribution diverges from deployment traffic, and the paper's negative result implies that minor deviations from its two stated conditions (dense attention unreachable by the gate, dense predictions as target) collapse the gate back to a no-op. 0 independent implementations, 125 stars. Research area: KV cache. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Embedding-Space Fingerprinting of LoRA Fine-Tunes: Recovering the Training-Data Domain from the Model Artifact Alone
item.description: The method replaces blind trust in LoRA artifacts with a lightweight classifier that identifies the training-data domain from weight deltas, internal activations, or generated text without accessing the original data. It costs only the extraction of feature vectors and training a simple classifier on known domains, requiring no cluster or foundation-model training. It can fail when encountering domains outside the five pre-registered categories, when base model architectures differ from Qwen3.5-0.8B, or when adversaries actively obfuscate these signals. 0 independent implementations, 125 stars. Research area: safety and guardrails. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Beyond Instruction Override: Benchmarking Indirect Prompt Injection with Task-Tampering Attacks
item.description: This benchmark replaces indirect prompt-injection evaluations that test planted instructions redirecting the agent toward an attacker-chosen task, instead defining attacks by unauthorized authority over decisions required by the benign task itself. It costs implementation effort to adapt the 90 validated cases across three tool-use environments to one's own agent architecture, plus inference costs for running evaluations across multiple models. After adoption, it can fail to surface vulnerabilities if the test cases do not cover the specific decision targets or tool schemas present in the production system, and defenses validated only on instruction-override benchmarks may appear more robust than they are against tampering attacks that manipulate values obtained during execution. 2 independent implementations, 2117 stars. Research area: safety and guardrails. Recommendation: test.

item.title: What the Middleman Delivers: Answer Behavior, Tool Permissions, and Billed Usage in LLM API Relays
item.description: The paper replaces implicit trust in advertised model names and listed prices with repeated empirical testing of third-party API relays for answer fidelity, tool-permission compliance, and billing accuracy. It costs engineering time to run batch-matched comparisons, repeated sampling, and account-balance checks, but no extra model infrastructure. It can fail if a relay changes behavior over time, if screening misses injected or altered content, or if billing discrepancies remain hidden where balances and reference token counts are unavailable. 0 independent implementations, 3 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: adopt.

item.title: English Calibration Erodes Lithuanian in Expert-Pruned Mixture-of-Experts Language Models
item.description: It replaces the common practice of pruning MoE experts with a single English calibration set by calibrating with Lithuanian or mixed Lithuanian-English data before REAP pruning. The cost is obtaining a representative target-language calibration set and running the pruning and evaluation once per language served, with no required increase in deployed model size. It can fail if the served language concentrates routing in a few late-layer experts that an English-only calibration marks unimportant, causing disproportionate target-language degradation. 0 independent implementations, 125 stars. Research area: sparsity and pruning. Recommendation: adopt.

item.title: Who Should Know What? Empirical Information Design for Multi-Agent LLM Economies
item.description: The framework replaces the default of giving every agent full or arbitrary context by systematically testing which information-sharing policy (ordinal vs. exact valuations, partial vs. full disclosure) each deployed model handles best, holding interaction rules fixed. It costs repeated simulation runs of the multi-agent market across candidate policies and models, plus engineering effort to implement configurable observation layers in the agent harness. It can fail because results are strongly model-dependent, so a policy tuned for one model may degrade outcomes after a model upgrade, and simulated market behavior may not transfer to the production task distribution. 1 independent implementation, 135 stars. Research area: multi-agent orchestration. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Instrumental Variables in Continuous-Time Stochastic Processes
item.description: The method replaces maximum-likelihood estimation and discrete-time IV approaches for identifying causal effects in continuous-time systems with unobserved confounding, using path-valued instruments and moment restrictions on SDE drift structure. Cost is moderate statistical and implementation complexity, including signature-kernel computation for nonlinear effects, but it runs on ordinary hardware. It can fail if the identification condition is unmet, if a valid instrumental process is unavailable, or if the stationarity and structural sparsity assumptions do not hold. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: MCPHallu: Benchmarking Reasoning, Execution, and Memory Hallucinations in MCP Agents
item.description: MCPHallu replaces aggregate task-completion scoring of MCP tool-using agents with a benchmark of 358 tasks on 36 containerized MCP servers, each task embedding a structural trigger targeting one hallucination subtype (Branch Collapse, Unreachable Goal, Tool Misuse, Context Forgetting) for subtype-level diagnosis. Adopting it costs the engineering effort to stand up the containerized MCP server environment, API or GPU spend to run agent trajectories, and integration work to map benchmark failures onto the reader's own tool configurations. The benchmark can fail to transfer if the reader's production tools, domains, or failure triggers differ from the 36 servers and five capability domains tested, and subtype rankings were shown to be unstable across models, so a single benchmark run may mischaracterize a model's behavior on a specific tool stack. 2 independent implementations, 138 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: test.

item.title: CAMP: Context-Aware Mapping and Placement for LLMs on 3D-IMC Arrays
item.description: Replaces prior weight-placement heuristics for 3D analog in-memory computing (AIMC) accelerators with a profiling-driven, context-aware mapping that accounts for MVM concurrency conflicts. The cost is an offline profiling and search loop plus a constraint on deploying to specialized 3D-IMC analog hardware; no model retraining is required. It fails outright without access to 3D-IMC chips, and its gains depend on the target architecture and runtime context, so results may not transfer across different AIMC designs or workloads. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: not applicable.

item.title: Automated Video-to-QA Pipeline: End-to-End Question Generation and Verification Using Large Language Models
item.description: The pipeline replaces manual QA annotation and ad hoc transcript review with a staged flow of FFmpeg audio extraction, Whisper transcription, BART chunk summarization, Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct QA drafting, self-verification filtering, and LoRA fine-tuning of the same model. On a single 24 GB GPU, the LoRA tuning step is feasible with quantized adapters, but the cascade adds preprocessing latency, storage for intermediate transcripts, orchestration complexity, and dependence on the quality of ASR and summaries. It can fail through transcription errors, summary information loss, verifier self-agreement, weak domain alignment, or synthetic QA drift that produces plausible but low-value assessment items. 0 independent implementations, 125 stars. Research area: efficient training. Recommendation: test.

item.title: ReConMem: A Graph-Based Dual Memory System for Repository-Oriented Conversations
item.description: Replaces flat conversational-history or generic RAG memory in repository-oriented assistants with a dual graph that links distilled conversation memories to code entities, using code-draft query grounding, graph expansion, and structure-aware compression. Costs include building and maintaining two graphs per session (entity extraction, embedding, cross-graph association updates), extra retrieval hops per turn, and implementation complexity beyond a standard vector-store pipeline. Failure modes include stale or incorrect entity-to-conversation links as the repository evolves, grounding failures when the generated code draft misidentifies the relevant entities, and retrieval noise from graph expansion that can exceed the compression gains. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: memory and context. Recommendation: test.

item.title: The Intrusion Pathway: How Non-Evidential Context Degrades Language Model Performance
item.description: The method replaces the default full attention computation under noisy, non-evidential context with a mask-level knockout of a small set of identified intrusion heads. It requires identifying those heads per model via activation analysis, adding a preprocessing step, and the ablation carries a bounded but nonzero cost to performance on helpful context. It can fail because head identification is model-specific, the 57% recovery is partial, and effectiveness on distractor types or tasks beyond the four evaluated is not established. 0 independent implementations, 125 stars. Research area: retrieval and RAG. Recommendation: test.

item.title: CORE: Coarse-to-Fine Search with Context Management for Deep Research
item.description: CORE replaces standard dense retrieval that returns full passages or naive truncation by leveraging token-level similarities from late-interaction rerankers to extract minimal relevant snippets and manage context expansion. It costs additional inference computation for the late-interaction reranker and introduces engineering complexity for context state management and snippet deduplication. The approach can fail if the coarse retriever misses relevant passages (preventing fine-grained recovery) or if snippet extraction severs critical contextual dependencies required for accurate reasoning. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: memory and context. Recommendation: adopt.

item.title: A Low Similarity Score Does Not Show Independence after Source-Conditioned Repository Rewriting
item.description: The technique replaces reliance on a single low token-similarity score as evidence that an LLM-assisted rewrite is independent, substituting repeated generations, threshold-spread reporting, and comparison against same-task independent implementations rather than unrelated projects. It costs only additional rewrite runs (usually under half an hour each per the paper) and the engineering effort to maintain a behavioural harness, with no new infrastructure or model requirements. It can fail if teams treat the repeated-run protocol as proof of independence rather than as a necessary but insufficient signal, since the paper shows no tested metric reliably separates conditioned rewrites from genuinely independent implementations. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: adopt.

item.title: AttnSR: Attention Step Reward for Long-Horizon Agentic RL
item.description: AttnSR replaces outcome-only terminal rewards in long-horizon agentic RL with step-level reward allocations derived from the policy's own attention graph, without a separately trained reward model or extra rollouts. Its costs are modest: attention-graph tracing during training replay, a running baseline for the terminal step, and integration into a PPO-style training loop rather than inference-time overhead. It can fail if policy attention is a poor proxy for step relevance, if rewards reinforce spurious intermediate steps, or if the single-model, two-environment results do not transfer to noisier tools, longer horizons, or different model families. 0 independent implementations, 1 star. Research area: efficient training. Recommendation: test.

item.title: CoRD: Coupled Rollouts Fill the Blind Spot of On-Policy Distillation
item.description: CoRD replaces the state distribution of standard on-policy distillation: instead of training the student purely on its own rollouts, it draws training states from a geometric interpolation of student and teacher via the maximal coupling of speculative decoding, substituting teacher tokens only where the student underweights the target. The cost is that both student and teacher distributions must be evaluated token-by-token during rollout generation (the same machinery as speculative decoding), adding teacher inference passes to data generation and implementation complexity, though interventions recede as the student improves. It can fail if the reader's pipeline relies on third-party APIs that do not expose token-level logits for both models (the coupling requires both distributions), if no suitable teacher of the same family is available, or if the workload is not a verifiable-reasoning task where the pass@1/pass@8 gains were demonstrated. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: distillation. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Compression Through a Context Lens: Evaluating Adaptation, Quantization, and Distillation in Arabic Legal LLMs
item.description: The technique replaces full-precision model weights (typically 16-bit) with 4-bit weights, and replaces a monolithic large teacher with a smaller distilled student if needed. It costs a small amount of accuracy (no-context drops of up to 3.2 percentage points for quantization, and generally declining accuracy with smaller distilled students) and adds deployment pipeline complexity. After adoption, the reliance on full-context prompting can mask internal knowledge collapse, meaning performance can fail unexpectedly when legal context is absent from the input. 0 independent implementations, 125 stars. Research area: quantization. Recommendation: adopt.

item.title: SEER: A Scalable Event-Driven Runtime for Parallel Execution of Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning Environments
item.description: SEER replaces the serial CPU-side env.step path of vectorized MARL environments with a bounded event-driven runtime using a CAS-based dual-layer queue and preflight-guided thread-pool sizing, so independent entity events execute in parallel while preserving serial-equivalent step semantics. Adoption costs a rewrite of the environment under an explicit event-locality contract (entity-local direct updates, cross-entity effects as ordered future events) plus the complexity of a custom parallel runtime, with no gain in memory or model quality. It can fail if the environment does not satisfy the locality contract, if workloads are not interaction-intensive enough to amortize scheduling overhead, or if subtle ordering bugs break serial-equivalence guarantees that training correctness depends on. 0 independent implementations, 10 stars. Research area: efficient training. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Reproducing Kernel (Quasi-)Banach Spaces with the $\ell^p$ Coefficient Norms
item.description: This paper provides a theoretical framework for kernel-based interpolation using non-convex ℓp quasi-norms (0<p<1) to promote sparsity, replacing standard convex ℓ1 or ℓ2 regularization in kernel methods. It requires solving non-convex optimization problems with careful parameter tuning and lacks evidence of scalability to large neural network architectures. The approach may fail to converge reliably due to non-convexity and offers no demonstrated advantage for typical deep learning workloads. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: not applicable.

item.title: Secure Formal Raising: Protecting the Development of AI through Executable Properties
item.description: The method replaces informal, runtime-enforced trust in tool calls, authorization, and data-flow checks with a formal raising environment that requires confirmed evidence and provenance before admission. It costs additional policy modeling, invariant checking, and integration complexity, with a plain-C reference implementation demonstrating feasibility but no production performance numbers. It can fail if real deployments cannot supply the required confirmed evidence, if the model omits relevant attacks beyond the proved invariants, or if the small reference setting does not scale to richer tool ecosystems. 0 independent implementations, 125 stars. Research area: safety and guardrails. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: DictLLM: Post-training Compression of Large Language Model with Dictionary Kernels
item.description: The method replaces dense weight matrices in grouped layers with a shared SVD-derived dictionary plus layer-specific sparse coefficients, both aggressively quantized using Hessian information, obtained without retraining. It costs a multi-step post-training optimization requiring Hessian and input-covariance estimation, and incurs a measurable perplexity increase (2.9 points on WikiText-2 at 5.1x compression). It can fail if grouped layers are not well suited to a shared dictionary, if sparse-coefficient storage and compute are not efficiently supported by the deployment runtime, or if zero-shot task degradation exceeds the reported averages on the reader's workload. 0 independent implementations, 125 stars. Research area: sparsity and pruning. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Gradient Boosting for Efficient Rank Discovery in Tensor Network Kernel Machines
item.description: GB-CPKM replaces explicit tensor-rank search via cross-validation over multiple candidate CP-rank models with sequential gradient boosting of fixed-rank learners, where ensemble size is chosen on validation performance. The cost is adoption of a niche tensor-network kernel formulation with its own implementation complexity, and gains are claimed only on regression benchmarks rather than deep learning workloads. It can fail when validation-based ensemble sizing overfits small validation sets, when the CP decomposition poorly fits the data structure, or when the workload does not benefit from kernel-machine modeling at all. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: efficient training. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Create Your Own Work Stack: Deploying Self-hosted AI and Tooling in a Tech Startup
item.description: The method replaces routing all development and coordination tasks to commercial AI agents with a hybrid stack where commercial models handle complex coding while self-hosted local models handle lower-complexity tasks, documentation synchronization, and retrieval from tools such as Outline, Plane, and ERPNext. It costs self-hosting infrastructure and integration effort, accepts that local models are insufficiently capable and fast for complex coding, and adds task-routing complexity; commercial cost savings are estimated rather than directly measured. Adoption can fail from UX friction if deployment is not centrally configured, and the savings depend entirely on whether a workload actually contains a large fraction of low-complexity coordination tasks. 0 independent implementations, 125 stars. Research area: multi-agent orchestration. Recommendation: test.

item.title: BUMP: Brief Unexpected Mid-Interpolation Peak
item.description: Replaces plain logit (prediction-space) ensembling of permutation-aligned model pairs with a hybrid scheme that also mixes weights near the interpolation endpoints, exploiting the brief accuracy peaks (BUMP) found there. Costs are modest: it requires at least two permutation-aligned models trained or fine-tuned from a shared init, plus endpoint weight interpolation and combined prediction mixing, adding storage for extra checkpoints and a small amount of offline search over interpolation coefficients. It can fail when models are not permutation-aligned (the peak depends on alignment), when the architecture or task falls outside the studied regimes, or when the near-endpoint gain does not survive the reader's specific data distribution, making the benefit workload-dependent. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: efficient architectures. Recommendation: test.

item.title: ProQuant: Progressive Quantization-aware Training for Edge MLLMs
item.description: ProQuant replaces post-training quantization (and prior QAT) for low-bit multimodal LLMs with a weight-activation QAT pipeline using self-relabeled training data and progressive block activation that prioritizes recovering multimodal understanding layers first. The cost is a full quantization-aware finetuning run with curated, self-relabeled data, which is substantially more compute- and engineering-intensive than PTQ methods such as GPTQ or AWQ and strains a single 24 GB GPU budget for 2B-8B vision-language models. Failure modes include distribution mismatch if the self-relabeling degrades data quality, reliance on the vision-sensitive layer identification generalizing to other architectures, and residual accuracy loss on tasks where the ~1% gap concentrates. 0 independent implementations, 125 stars. Research area: quantization. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Agent-R$^2$: Scaling Agents for Realistic Productivity Work via Real-Source Data Synthesis
item.description: This method replaces manually specified workflows or LLM-generated files with a real-source data synthesis framework grounded in real occupational seeds and web-sourced files. It costs significant infrastructure to execute the data distillation pipeline and the subsequent supervised fine-tuning and rubric-based reinforcement learning. It can fail if the specific web-corpus candidates do not generalize to the user's domain or if the rubric-based evaluation introduces biases. 1 independent implementation, 135 stars. Research area: efficient training. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: "Blind Compliance": Coercive Control in AI Jailbreaking
item.description: The paper replaces output-focused jailbreak detection with an interaction-centered framework that maps persona-based attacks onto coercive control categories drawn from interpersonal violence scholarship, treating jailbreaking as a relational dynamic rather than a classical exploit. It costs no compute or infrastructure since it is an analytical lens rather than a deployable defense, but operationalizing it would require building new classifiers or annotation schemes around conversational patterns rather than final outputs. It can fail in practice because the framework offers no validated detection method, benchmark, or measurable reduction in jailbreak success rates, so adopting it as a sole basis for guardrail design would be premature. 0 independent implementations, 2116 stars. Research area: safety and guardrails. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: From Twisted Facts to Rogue Agents: Can LLMs Reliably Detect Multi-Dimensional Hallucinations?
item.description: Replaces ad hoc or narrow hallucination checks with a bilingual benchmark spanning factual text and agent-trajectory faithfulness errors with fine-grained annotations. Costs are limited to evaluation compute and annotation access, but adopting it requires maintaining benchmark infrastructure rather than deploying a detection method. The benchmark itself does not solve hallucination detection and may not transfer to domain-specific production failure modes. 1 independent implementation, 135 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Terminal-style Mathematical Modeling Bench: The First Agentic and Verifiable Benchmark for Mathematical Modeling
item.description: TB-MathModel replaces LLM-judged report grading and solver-fragment scoring with containerized, terminal-based tasks whose JSON answers are checked against reproductions of Outstanding-award papers, using one-sided direction-aware scoring, a programmatic feasibility gate over six invariant forms, and 624 Lean 4 obligations that zero infeasible answers. Adoption costs building or pulling the provided containers and Lean toolchain, plus per-run agent API or GPU inference expense; the benchmark itself is evaluation infrastructure, not a deployable model improvement. It can fail as a production signal because it covers only 18 contest problems, anchors correctness to specific reference solutions that may not generalize to the reader's domain, and the hard feasibility gate depends on the completeness of hand-written invariants and Lean obligations. 1 independent implementation, 140 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: AutoCompress: Automated Hardware-Guided Model Compression
item.description: Replaces manual parameter-count-based pruning and heuristic model resizing with automated, hardware-aware differentiable architecture search guided by serving-engine cost models. Requires integration with specific serving engines and hardware profiling infrastructure, plus computational resources for the search phase that likely exceed a single 24GB GPU for large models. Post-adoption risks include dependency on proprietary cost models that may not generalize to different hardware or engine versions, and the method may be inaccessible without the authors' specific infrastructure. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: sparsity and pruning. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Should You Split Decode? Disaggregation Across Future Models and Accelerators
item.description: The paper compares prefill/decode disaggregation against further attention/FFN disaggregation for LLM inference serving. It finds no robust deployment-level advantage for the finer split in SLO goodput per kW, while AFD adds communication overhead, placement constraints, and a third provisioned resource pool; any nominal lead typically stems from fitting an extra prefill replica rather than a more efficient decode pool. The approach fails if hardware mappings are fixed early, as advantages disappear when models, fabrics, or objectives change. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: serving and batching. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: GINGER: Spicing Up Graph-Based Vector Search
item.description: Ginger replaces existing approximate nearest neighbor search libraries (such as HNSW implementations) with a graph-based index built on PiPNN construction, Nested TurboQuant two-level vector quantization, and AdaptiveGap graph compression. It is an open-source C++ library requiring CPU-based index construction and memory for the compressed graph and quantized vectors; integration effort and build complexity are the main costs, with memory reduced 2.6x versus float32 vectors and graph size reduced up to 2.5x. Adoption can fail if recall targets above 95% are required, if the dataset is small enough that brute force is sufficient, or if integration with existing vector-serving infrastructure adds unacceptable engineering overhead. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: retrieval and RAG. Recommendation: adopt.

item.title: Learning the Task or Learning the Verifier? Rethinking Criteria Exposure in Embodied Self-Improvement
item.description: This diagnostic practice replaces the direct exposure of benchmark verification criteria (CE) to the learning agent with instruction-faithful criteria designed to strictly match task language. It costs additional engineering effort to design and validate robust evaluation protocols without reducing model inference latency or compute requirements. Success metrics can still overfit to specific criterion phrasing, and improved scores may not transfer to slightly perturbed verification conditions. 2 independent implementations, 155 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: test.

item.title: StrataFlux: Memory-Hierarchy-Native Low-Bit LLM Inference
item.description: StrataFlux replaces pure GPU-resident low-bit quantization by storing refinement precision in host RAM and SSD and streaming selected higher-precision components to recover accuracy without giving up quantization's memory and speed benefits. The cost is added system complexity: precision selection logic, transfer overlap scheduling, and reuse management across decoding steps, plus dependence on host memory bandwidth and storage latency. Failure modes include degraded gains when host-to-GPU bandwidth is insufficient, when the precision selection policy mispredicts which components matter, and when integration with existing inference stacks (vLLM, TensorRT-LLM) proves non-trivial outside the evaluated platforms. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: quantization. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Muir: Linear Attention with Sensitivity-Allocated Gating and Matched-Filter Readout
item.description: This method replaces the full-rank erase and write gates in Gated DeltaNet-2 with a sensitivity-allocated low-rank projection and a matched-filter readout gate. It requires implementing a novel parallel chunkwise update algorithm to maintain numerical stability during training, which introduces significant engineering complexity and risk. The technique has only been validated at 1.34B parameters; it is unproven at the larger scales typically required for production foundation models, and custom kernels may not be available or optimized for consumer-grade 24GB GPUs. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: efficient architectures. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: SCALE: Real-Time Latent Communication for Cyber-Physical Agents
item.description: SCALE replaces transmission of full latent messages or raw sensor data between cyber-physical agents with a scheduler that reuses matched tokens from prior messages and transmits only a budgeted subset of latent tokens chosen by profiled semantic gain versus communication cost. It costs an online token-matching stage, per-message semantic/cost profiling, and a real-time scheduling component, plus an anonymous-repository codebase whose maturity is unverified; quality degrades gracefully only insofar as the profiles are accurate. It can fail when scene dynamics break the assumed spatio-temporal continuity (making token reuse stale or wrong), when semantic-gain profiles misestimate task utility under shifting deadlines, or when the reader's workload is LLM-agent orchestration rather than bandwidth-constrained embodied multi-agent communication. 0 independent implementations, 10 stars. Research area: multi-agent orchestration. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Spectral and Subspace Dynamics of LoRA in Supervised Fine-Tuning and Reinforcement Learning
item.description: The method replaces uniform, stage-agnostic LoRA updates in SFT and RL with stage-specific spectral shaping: flattening the spectrum of the full update in SFT, and flattening only the component outside the current LoRA increment span in RL to encourage subspace rotation. It costs a singular value decomposition (or equivalent subspace computation) of the LoRA update at each step or interval, plus implementation complexity in the optimizer loop; memory overhead is modest since LoRA increments are small. It can fail if the underlying diagnosis—driven by group-mean baseline subtraction in RL—does not transfer to other tasks, reward designs, or base models, and the gains may shrink for workloads whose dynamics differ from the mathematical-reasoning tasks studied. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: efficient training. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Benchmarks as Software: Terminal-Bench and the Case for Continuous Benchmarks
item.description: The workflow replaces one-time, release-and-freeze benchmark curation with continuous validation combining community reports, agent traces, automated oracle checks, and human-gated repairs, plus explicit validation of resource budgets such as wall-clock limits. It costs ongoing human review effort, re-running of evaluations after repairs, and added infrastructure for trace collection and oracle checks, all feasible on a single GPU or via APIs since only agents are executed, not trained. It can fail if human gating becomes a bottleneck, if repairs are inconsistent or introduce new verifier biases, or if revalidated resource settings are not reported, making scores incomparable across evaluations. 0 independent implementations, 125 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: adopt.

item.title: The Power of Meta Access in the Software of the Future --- Demonstrated on LLM Chat UIs and Chat AI
item.description: The technique replaces fragmented navigation, settings manipulation, and workspace organization with structured, permissioned assistant access to application state. It costs additional context engineering, permission boundaries, and UI-state metamodel exposure rather than extra model capacity. It can fail through grounding errors, privacy leakage, prompt injection, and unsafe mutations if confirmation and reversibility are weak. 0 independent implementations, 125 stars. Research area: tool use. Recommendation: test.

item.title: ReproBridge: Building Reproducibility into ML Research Artifacts
item.description: Replaces ad-hoc interpretation of scattered research artifacts—raw code, papers, and supplementary materials—with a structured reproducibility package comprising refined codebase, environment specifications, experiment launchers, and documented procedures. Costs include an initial agent-driven construction phase to generate the refined artifacts and ongoing maintenance to keep them synchronized with upstream changes. Failure modes include artifacts becoming outdated as underlying libraries evolve, propagation of errors if the initial artifact generation contains subtle inaccuracies, and residual dependence on agent capability for edge cases not covered by the standardized components. 0 independent implementations, 125 stars. Research area: coding agents. Recommendation: adopt.

item.title: A low-rank decoder bottleneck bounds reliability in foundation-model perturbation prediction
item.description: The method replaces per-prediction trust in foundation-model perturbation response outputs with a calibrated confidence score, the cosine distance from a predicted response to its nearest training response, motivated by the finding that the ST decoder's first attention layer is low-rank (projecting onto 4-32 fixed directions preserves mean PDC). It requires storing training response vectors and computing nearest-neighbor cosine distances per prediction, plus calibration data to set thresholds; the underlying model and decoder are unchanged, so no retraining or extra GPU capacity is needed. It can fail when predictions are reliable but far from all training responses (false low confidence), when the training set poorly covers the test distribution, and its validation is specific to the STATE ST decoder and CRISPRi/drug perturbation settings, so transfer to other architectures or assay types is unverified. 1 independent implementation, 4 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Modality-Aware Expert Pruning for MoE-Based Multimodal Large Language Models
item.description: MAEP replaces modality-agnostic expert-pruning importance metrics with a training-free, single-forward-pass metric that separates vision-side pruning signals from text-side preservation signals for MoE-based MLLMs. Cost is limited to a calibration forward pass and permanent removal of experts, with no retraining; inference speed is largely unchanged since it removes parameters rather than adding compute. It can fail when the workload's vision-token statistics differ from those used for calibration, when the low-attention vision-token assumption breaks on a new domain, or when text-heavy tasks suffer because text importance was only a preservation signal rather than the optimization target. 1 independent implementation, 129 stars. Research area: sparsity and pruning. Recommendation: adopt.

item.title: Phantom: Temporal Caching for Diffusion Models
item.description: Phantom replaces full diffusion computation by reusing cached activations and recomputing only tokens that change significantly between timesteps. The approach requires specialized systolic-array hardware additions, making it inaccessible to standard GPU or API deployments. The method may fail if outlier detection degrades image quality or if hardware-specific assumptions do not transfer to commodity accelerators. 0 independent implementations, 4 stars. Research area: attention and kernels. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: SysPilot: Cross-Library Performance Autotuning via Library Performance Contracts
item.description: The method replaces application-specific manual tuning and general-purpose autotuners with reusable Library Performance Contracts that encode resource demands and observability signals across libraries. It requires contract synthesis from documentation and code artifacts plus profiling runs to validate conflict hypotheses, which adds specification and instrumentation complexity. It can fail when contracts are incomplete or inaccurate, when contention patterns shift across deployments, or when the target libraries lack sufficient observability to validate the derived hypotheses. 1 independent implementation, 5 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: TauLang: A Language and Compiler for Space-Time Programming on Statically Scheduled Accelerators
item.description: TauLang replaces implicit, hardware-resolved scheduling in conventional kernel languages with explicit parameterized time annotations, validated algebraically and solved jointly with tensor placement via an integer linear program. The cost is a new language and compiler toolchain plus ILP solve time, and it presupposes a statically scheduled accelerator such as a Groq TSP rather than a GPU. It fails to apply when the target hardware has dynamic scheduling (caches, arbiters, hardware schedulers), and schedule validity depends on compiler correctness since mistimed operations are correctness errors, not performance regressions. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: attention and kernels. Recommendation: not applicable.

item.title: Shallow Encoding Emits Deep Memories
item.description: The technique replaces full-depth prefill with a shallow emitter that writes deep-layer memories from an earlier anchor layer, and replaces full recurrent-state storage with a fixed sink direction plus low-rank factors. It keeps the original weights frozen and does not compress the attention cache, but requires hybrid architectures with recurrent states and support for exact low-rank state updates in the serving stack. Quality risk is bounded but real: the method is only validated on six checkpoints of production hybrids, and the throughput gain depends on workloads with long prompts or agentic traces. 0 independent implementations, 4 stars. Research area: serving and batching. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: FaCoDiff: Factor-Correlated Diffusion for Multivariate Probabilistic Forecasting
item.description: Replaces dense covariance estimation or diagonal-noise diffusion models for multivariate probabilistic forecasting with a low-rank factor structure that preserves marginal variances while modeling cross-variable dependence. Costs include implementing a conditional statistical estimator, diagonal compensation mechanics, and a geometry-aware diffusion objective, though the method avoids O(N³) dense matrix operations. Can fail if the low-rank factor assumption does not capture true cross-variable dependence in your specific time series, or if the implementation complexity of the coupled estimator-denoiser introduces integration overhead disproportionate to accuracy gains over simpler baselines. 0 independent implementations, 4 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: CARE-FL: Federated Fine-Tuning of Multimodal LLMs in Resource-Constrained Edge Networks
item.description: The method replaces heuristic or random client selection in federated LoRA fine-tuning of multimodal LLMs with a Double Deep Q-Learning selector using Q-value decomposition, constraint-aware epsilon-greedy subset selection, and an adaptive aggregation rule that can upweight the previous global model. It costs the engineering complexity of running an online RL selector and per-round utility estimation on top of the federated orchestration, plus the overhead of tracking latency and bandwidth feasibility each round. It can fail if the online-learned utilities misestimate client value under shifting data or system conditions, if the emulated wireless setting does not transfer to real deployments, or if the adaptive aggregation stalls convergence by overweighting stale models. 0 independent implementations, 4 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: not applicable.

item.title: Editing Large Language Models with Geometry-Aware Regularization
item.description: GEdit replaces unconstrained knowledge-editing methods (such as ROME/MEMIT-style weight updates and their sequential variants) with an LR+D factor model of FFN hidden representations that protects a low-rank core knowledge subspace and adapts regularization strength per edit difficulty. The cost is additional per-edit computation to estimate the representation geometry and calibrate editability, plus implementation complexity over existing editing libraries. It can fail if the assumed low-rank structure does not hold for a given model, if editability is miscalibrated (hard edits fail or easy edits corrupt pretrained knowledge), or if the method's benefits do not transfer beyond the evaluated GPT2-XL/GPT-J/LLaMA-3-8B settings. 1 independent implementation, 129 stars. Research area: efficient training. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Zuse: A Decision Model for European Languages
item.description: Replaces generative classification (prompting an LLM to output a label) with a fixed-set classifier that returns calibrated probabilities over options, trained via a low-rank adapter plus pointer head on frozen open-weight bases (4B, 9B, 27B). The 4B and 9B variants fit a 24 GB GPU for both adapter training and inference; costs are the adapter training pipeline, per-task calibration checks, and base-model dependence. Miscalibration varies by task (knowledge overconfident, acceptability underconfident) so no single temperature fixes all tasks; performance collapses 23-28 points in languages outside the base model's documented list, training data is vulnerable to label-word collisions and augmentation shortcuts, and English results lag competing models (Jev, Kev). 1 independent implementation, 129 stars. Research area: efficient training. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Analysis of Local Open-Weight LLM Agents on Vulnerability-Reproduction Tasks
item.description: This approach replaces sending proprietary code to hosted security-analysis APIs with locally-run open-weight models (4B–27B parameters) that autonomously generate crash-inducing inputs from vulnerability descriptions. The cost includes GPU memory sufficient for 27B-scale models (within 24 GB at appropriate quantization), slower wall-clock convergence compared to mixture-of-experts variants, and engineering effort to build execution harnesses that compile and run target code. Failure occurs when models correctly identify vulnerable functions and state hypotheses but cannot synthesize working exploit inputs, particularly on harder tasks where only 27B models succeed. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: coding agents. Recommendation: test.

item.title: A.S.E 2.0: Understanding How Repository Context Impacts the Security of LLM-Generated Code
item.description: The technique replaces default functionality-oriented context construction (standard retrieval, file ranking, agent-driven exploration) with security-aware context construction that explicitly surfaces safeguard code and excludes insecure exemplars before generation. It costs additional engineering to identify and annotate security-relevant repository elements per project, plus modest retrieval overhead, and provides no runtime latency change since it affects only context assembly. It can fail when safeguard locations are misidentified, when the model ignores injected safeguards, or when the security-relevant code is too dispersed across the repository to fit the context window. 0 independent implementations, 3 stars. Research area: coding agents. Recommendation: test.

item.title: MA-Mesh: Resilient Multi-Agent Collaboration via Role-based Self-Healing
item.description: This technique replaces ad-hoc output correction and static role assignment with a runtime self-healing layer that uses cross-agent reflection and dynamic role-based failover.
